classification.difficultyReason: Construct complete similarity proofs using parallel-line angle relationships and correctly ordered vertices.

content.prompt: Explain why these triangles are similar. Show full reasoning.

spec.description: Intersecting straight lines D–E–F and C–E–G with matching single parallel arrows on CD and FG. Ordinary source strokes are rendered black in house style; no shading.
spec.mathematics: D, E, F are collinear; C, E, G are collinear; CD is parallel to FG. The compared triangles are CDE and GFE.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and labels are visible; no proof or answer annotations.

answer.short: $\triangle CDE\sim\triangle GFE$: $\angle DCE=\angle FGE$ and $\angle CDE=\angle GFE$ (alternate angles on parallel lines). At least two pairs of equal corresponding angles.
answer.worked:
$\angle DCE=\angle FGE$ (alternate angles, $CD\parallel FG$).

$\angle CDE=\angle GFE$ (alternate angles, $CD\parallel FG$).

Therefore $\triangle CDE\sim\triangle GFE$, since at least two pairs of corresponding angles are equal (AAA).

spec.description: Nested triangles with L at lower left, M at upper left and N at right. Matching single parallel arrows point left on MN and QP. Ordinary strokes are black and the figure is unshaded.
spec.mathematics: L, Q, M are collinear; L, P, N are collinear; QP is parallel to MN. The compared triangles are LQP and LMN.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and labels are visible; no proof or answer annotations.

answer.short: $\triangle LQP\sim\triangle LMN$: $\angle QLP=\angle MLN$ (common angle) and $\angle LQP=\angle LMN$ (corresponding angles on parallel lines). At least two pairs of equal corresponding angles.
answer.worked:
$\angle QLP=\angle MLN$ (common angle at $L$).

$\angle LQP=\angle LMN$ (corresponding angles, $QP\parallel MN$).

Therefore $\triangle LQP\sim\triangle LMN$, since at least two pairs of corresponding angles are equal (AAA).

spec.description: Nested triangles with W upper left, Y upper right and U below W. Matching single parallel arrows point upward along VX and UY. Ordinary strokes are black and the figure is unshaded.
spec.mathematics: W, V, U are collinear; W, X, Y are collinear; VX is parallel to UY. The compared triangles are WVX and WUY.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and labels are visible; no proof or answer annotations.

answer.short: $\triangle WVX\sim\triangle WUY$: $\angle VWX=\angle UWY$ (common angle) and $\angle WVX=\angle WUY$ (corresponding angles on parallel lines). At least two pairs of equal corresponding angles.
answer.worked:
$\angle VWX=\angle UWY$ (common angle at $W$).

$\angle WVX=\angle WUY$ (corresponding angles, $VX\parallel UY$).

Therefore $\triangle WVX\sim\triangle WUY$, since at least two pairs of corresponding angles are equal (AAA).
